summary: The Digby tower (indexed as Dibgy): a wooden tower from 1922, replaced by steel in 1957, out of service by the late 1960s; the site is now mostly swamp.

facts.design: 30.5 m (100 ft) heavy steel tower, built in 1957 to replace a wooden tower
facts.status_note: Taken out of service in the late 1960s; no source says whether any part of the tower remains.

access.note: The township's Wikipedia article says the area is mostly swamp and can be reached by a newer private road to the west.

events.note: First wooden tower on the site, per the Lindsay Fire District tower notes
30.5 m (100 ft) heavy steel tower replaced the wooden tower

sources.title: Ontario Fire Towers (tower history notes, Tweed and Lindsay fire districts)

notes_for_editor: Location conflict: the Firelookout.ca record (Sebright, 44.69534, -79.16457) does not match the township article, which puts the old tower north of Uphill in the former Laxton, Digby and Longford Township. Not corrected: the township article gives no tower coordinates, so a human should check the point. The Wikipedia article says it cites no sources, so its late-1960s date and swamp/road statement are uncited. 'Late 1960s' is not a single year, so no decommissioning event was written. The GeoCities page is a fan-run archive with no named author or agency. The cached Ontario LIO layer in data/raw has no feature with these names. The name correction (Dibgy to Digby) is proposed for a human to review. Checked 2026-10-20 on the full GeoCities page: the Digby entry sits under the Lindsay Fire District heading, which is formed in the 1940s.
